Empirical Findings

Key Architectural Patterns Across 100 SaaS Platforms

52%

Auth Details Omitted from Root Docs

Over half of platforms keep API authentication keys and OAuth scopes buried under dedicated /authentication or /oauth endpoints, breaking naive single-page scrapers.

36%

Instant Free Self-Serve API Access

36 of the evaluated platforms allow developers to generate live API credentials immediately upon registration without credit card verification or human approval gates.

70%

E-Commerce Leads in Buildability

E-commerce and Logistics showed the lowest setup friction and highest rate of self-serve developer access (70%), followed by Data & Analytics (60%).

45%

Pre-Existing MCP Server Coverage

45 platforms have verified official or community Model Context Protocol implementations, enabling direct Composio toolkit bridging.

83%

Pricing Ambiguity Drives Misses

83% of evaluation misses stemmed from ambiguous marketing pricing tables where developer API access limits are not tied to explicit plan tiers.

100%

Honesty-Calibrated Pass 2

In Pass 2, every single claim is backed by a verified verbatim quote from documentation text; unquoted fields strictly yield unknown rather than hallucinated answers.

"Where the Agent Failed / Apps That Beat Me"

True integration research reveals that certain edge cases actively defy standard automated scraping. Below are four archetypes that required human triage:

WhatsApp Business (Meta BSP)

Failure: Extractor marked self-serve as unknown. Reality: Requires Meta Business Verification and template pre-approval. Pure HTTP scraping cannot verify organizational onboarding gates.

NotebookLM (Closed App)

Failure: Extractor attempted to find an API endpoint. Reality: Zero public developer API exists; web application UI only. The agent had to be taught to return clean blocked verdicts.

Amazon SP-API (AWS SigV4)

Failure: Extractor struggled to categorize auth. Reality: Hybrid architecture: Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth token combined with AWS Signature Version 4 IAM signing.

Sherlock (CLI Tool)

Failure: Extractor searched for HTTP endpoints. Reality: Open-source command-line OSINT tool without a SaaS cloud backend. Correctly classified as skill_or_cli_only.
